subject: Environment fit evaluation — identity, encryption & audit plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@synthex.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + clarifying questions (identity / keys / retention)

Elena — thanks for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a few clarifying items that will determine whether Synthex should plan for Redwood Dedicated or Redwood Private:

- Primary drivers we heard: customer-managed key custody for inference models, SCIM + SAML SSO integration across multiple teams, and 7+ years of immutable audit logs for compliance.
- Timelines: you noted a procurement decision window by end of Q1 2027 and a pilot aiming for Q2.

Clarifying questions we need answered to recommend a hosting path (short answers are fine):
1) KMS/HSM: Do you require an on-prem HSM (Thales/Entrust) or cloud HSM (Azure Key Vault Managed HSM / AWS CloudHSM) with BYOK? Or is integration with Redwood-managed KMS acceptable if keys are customer-wrapped?
2) SSO: Is SAML-only acceptable or do you require OIDC + SCIM provisioning? Any IdPs we should verify (Okta, Azure AD, Ping)?
3) Logs & retention: You mentioned long-term retention. Is the 7+ year retention mandatory for all inference logs, or only for audit summaries/metadata? Any specific log encryption or WORM requirements?
4) Data residency & network: Do you need VPC/VNet peering and no public egress from instances? Any requirements for air-gapped/on‑prem components?

Next steps I propose: once you confirm the items above, we’ll schedule a 60-minute technical workshop with Ben (solutions) and our infra engineer to map a concrete architecture and note any contract-level redlines for procurement. I’ll also attach a short compliance matrix template you can fill in.

Attachments: synthex-compliance-matrix.xlsx (empty template we discussed)

Thanks — Karthik
--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@synthex.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@synthex.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + clarifying questions (identity / keys / retention)

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. Answers inline: 

1) KMS/HSM: We must have customer-controlled HSM. Preferred is Azure Key Vault Managed HSM for the cloud pilot; long term we may move to an on-prem Thales HSM for FIPS 140-2 Level 3 certified custody. BYOK with HSM-backed keys is required.
2) SSO: Okta is our primary IdP. We need SAML for SSO and SCIM to provision/deprovision service accounts. OIDC is nice-to-have but not required for MVP.
3) Logs & retention: Regulatory team requires 7 years for audit-relevant metadata and 1 year for raw debug logs. All retained logs must be tamper-evident (WORM-like) and encrypted at rest with customer keys.
4) Data residency & network: For the pilot we can use US-region cloud with VNet peering and private endpoints; production for regulated workloads will likely require VPC-private deployment (no public egress).

I attached our filled compliance matrix and a short note from procurement outlining required contract clauses (SLA, data handling, indemnity).

Attachments: synthex-compliance-matrix.xlsx

Elena
Elena Morales
Head of IT Security | Synthex AI
elena.morales@synthex.ai | +1 (212) 555-0999

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@synthex.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 13:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + clarifying questions (identity / keys / retention)

Elena — thanks for the fast answers and the matrix. Technical notes from our side (high level):

- HSM / KMS: Your Azure Managed HSM BYOK requirement is supported, and we can integrate Redwood Dedicated with Azure Key Vault Managed HSM using customer-managed keys. For Thales on-prem HSMs, that triggers the Private (VPC or on-prem bundle) recommendation because it requires either a direct HSM appliance integration or an HSM proxy in the customer VPC.
- SSO & SCIM: We have a supported Okta SAML + SCIM flow for provisioning service accounts and roles. We’ll bring a SCIM connector template to the workshop; full sync/cycle times will need testing for your org size.
- Log retention & WORM: We can satisfy 7-year metadata retention by exporting deduplicated audit records to a customer-managed object store (S3/GCS/Azure Blob) with enforced retention policies (immutability). For tamper-evidence, we recommend signed object manifests and storage-level immutability (eg Azure Blob Immutable Storage / AWS S3 Object Lock).
- Network/residency: For the pilot, Redwood Dedicated with VNet peering + private endpoint should be OK. For the regulated production path (on-prem HSM + no public egress), Redwood Private (customer VPC or installed on-prem appliance) is the safe path.

Recommended immediate plan:
1) Short architecture workshop (60 min) to validate network & HSM integration approach and confirm SCIM provisioning scope.
2) Small pilot: Dedicated in your Azure region with Managed HSM BYOK + log export to a customer-controlled blob with 1-year retention for raw logs and 7-year retention for audit metadata.
3) Long-term: plan for Private deployment if/when you adopt on-prem HSM and require zero public egress.

I attached a concise one-pager comparing Dedicated vs Private for HSM/SSO/retention takeaways. Happy to walk through this in the workshop.

Attachments: redwood-private-checklist.pdf

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

I’ll prepare a ballpark commercial for the pilot (Dedicated capacity) so procurement has numbers for the Q1 decision. Karthik — if you can include a checklist of the deliverables we’ll cover in the workshop, that will help keep the call focused.
